title: Third water line commissioned at Sheikhupura
description: A third bottling line lifts drinking-water capacity to 60,000 bottles a day ahead of the summer peak.
content:
We have commissioned a third drinking-water bottling line at the Sheikhupura plant, taking water capacity from 38,000 to 60,000 bottles a day.
The line handles 500 ml and 1.5 L PET and runs off the same reverse-osmosis and UV train as the existing two, with an added 0.2 micron final filter stage. Commissioning took eleven weeks, and the line entered commercial production on 1 July.
Why now The expansion was driven by demand from Lahore and Gujranwala, where summer orders had been running roughly 30% ahead of what the previous two lines could fill. Through May and June we were allocating rather than filling orders, which is not a position we want to be in during the months that matter most.
What changes for distributors 500 ml case availability improves immediately in Punjab (North) 19 L returnable delivery in Sheikhupura and Lahore moves from thrice- to four-times weekly from August No change to trade prices this quarter Distributors with questions about revised allocations should contact their regional manager.

title: Mango intake for 2026 closes 12% above last season
description: Contracted pulp from Multan and Rahim Yar Khan comes in ahead of plan despite a late start.
content:
This year’s mango pulp intake closed at 12% above the 2025 season, despite a start delayed by roughly two weeks in the Rahim Yar Khan belt.
We contract pulp ahead of the season rather than buying spot, and this year’s contracts covered 68 growers across Multan and Rahim Yar Khan districts — nine more than last year.
Why it matters for the product Pulp bought on contract comes from the same orchards year after year, which is what keeps the flavour of Naail Mango Nectar consistent from batch to batch. Spot-market pulp varies far more in Brix and colour, and the difference is noticeable in the glass.
Contracting early costs us flexibility on price. What it buys is a product that tastes the same in March as it did in July.
Production plan Peak nectar production runs June through September. We expect to hold 40% pulp content across the full season with no reformulation, and to carry sufficient aseptic pulp stock into the first quarter of 2027.

title: ISO 22000 recertified through 2028
description: The Sheikhupura plant clears its three-year food safety recertification audit with no major findings.
content:
The Sheikhupura plant has been recertified to ISO 22000:2018 following a three-day audit in April, with the certificate now valid through August 2028.
The audit covered all six production lines, the in-house laboratory, incoming material control and the snack hall. It closed with no major non-conformities and two minor observations, both relating to documentation rather than process.
Observations and response Retention sample log format — the log did not consistently record the storage temperature at the point of filing. We have moved the log to a fixed template with temperature as a required field. Supplier re-approval intervals — two concentrate suppliers were past their scheduled re-approval date. Both have since been re-approved and the review calendar is now on a quarterly reminder. Both were closed out within thirty days of the audit.
Current certification status Certification Valid through ISO 22000:2018 Aug 2028 ISO 9001:2015 Aug 2028 HACCP Mar 2027 PSQCA licence Dec 2027 Halal certification Jun 2027
